dd​t​S​(Φt​(ρ))+αt​S​(Φt​(ρ))≥dd​t​S​(τxt)+αt​S​(τxt).\frac{\text{\rm{d}}}{\text{\rm{d}}t}S\big(\Phi_{t}(\rho)\big)+\alpha_{t}S(\Phi_{t}(\rho))\geq\frac{\text{\rm{d}}}{\text{\rm{d}}t}S(\tau_{x_{t}})+\alpha_{t}S(\tau_{x_{t}}).

Taking the integral of both sides yields

S⁡(Φt1​(ρ))−S⁡(Φt0​(ρ))+∫t0t1αt​S​(Φt​(ρ))​d​t≥S⁡(τxt1)−S⁡(τxt0)+∫t0t1αt​S​(τxt)​d​t.\displaystyle S\big(\Phi_{t_{1}}(\rho)\big)-S\big(\Phi_{t_{0}}(\rho)\big)+\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\!\alpha_{t}S(\Phi_{t}(\rho))\,\text{\rm{d}}t\geq S(\tau_{x_{t_{1}}})-S(\tau_{x_{t_{0}}})+\int_{t_{0}}^{t_{1}}\!\alpha_{t}S(\tau_{x_{t}})\,\text{\rm{d}}t.

We note that S⁡(Φt0​(ρ))=S⁡(τxt0)S(\Phi_{t_{0}}(\rho))=S(\tau_{x_{t_{0}}}), so this inequality is in contradiction with (50). This implies that the starting inequality S⁡(Φt1​(ρ))<S⁡(Φt1​(τx0))S\big(\Phi_{t_{1}}(\rho)\big)<S(\Phi_{t_{1}}(\tau_{x_{0}})) does not hold.

∎

Generalization of the CMOE conjecture to the multimode case is an open problem in general. However, generalizing the proof idea of Theorem 11 and using Theorem 3, we can prove the conjecture for a special class of multimode states that can be prepared by applying a passive Gaussian unitary UGU_{G} on an arbitrary product state, ρ=UGρ1⊗ρ2⊗⋯⊗ρmUG†\rho=U_{G}\rho_{1}\otimes\rho_{2}\otimes\cdots\otimes\rho_{m}U_{G}^{\dagger}.

6 Conclusion

In this paper, we introduced a meta log-Sobolev inequality, formalized by Theorem 1, that provides a general information theoretic framework to study phase-covariant Gaussian quantum channels. In general, this inequality and our technical proof, particularly the tensorization argument that we used in the second step, are of independent interest. However, by using this result, we have derived new optimal bounds in the context of pp-log-Sobolev inequalities for the semigroup of attenuation channels.

Specifically, in Theorem 4, we explicitly computed the optimal pp-log-Sobolev constant of the quantum Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup for any 1≤p≤21\leq p\leq 2. We also in Theorem 10 established a bound on the 22-log-Sobolev constant in the multimode case that scales logarithmically with the number of modes. We conjecture that the log-Sobolev constants in the multimode case match those of the single-mode case and the tensorization property holds in general. We showed in Corollary 6 that this conjecture holds assuming that the optimal multimode states are Gaussian.

Quantum log-Sobolev inequalities are also defined for 0≤p<10\leq p<1 and are related to reverse hypercontractivity inequalities [10, 2]. An interesting open problem is to compute the pp-log-Sobolev constant for this range of parameter, which we leave it for future works.

The proof of our multimode log-Sobolev inequality is based on an entropic inequality in Lemma 9 which is of independent interest. Using this inequality, one might be able to prove log-Sobolev inequalities for the tensor product of other quantum Markov semigroups. We leave exploration of such applications of Lemma 9 for future works.

Our results have novel consequences even in the fully classical case, i.e., when restricting to states ρ\rho that are diagonal in the Fock basis. In particular, as pointed out in [6], restricting the quantum Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup to diagonal states, we obtain a classical birth-death process whose log-Sobolev constants were not known prior to our work (except in the case of p=1p=1). Moreover, our results have consequences for the classical operation of thinning on the space of integer-valued random variables, for which we refer to [18] and references therein.

We also presented an alternative proof of the CMOE conjecture in Theorem 11 in the single-mode case. This conjecture in the multimode case is left as a major open problem. Our results contribute to the resolution of Gaussian optimizer conjectures in the quantum case [18]. These conjectures state the optimality of Gaussian states for certain optimization problems regarding Gaussian channels. Theorem 1 establishes this conjecture for the quite general function Υ⁡(ρ)\Upsilon(\rho) in the single-mode case. Generalizing this theorem for multimode states can resolve the CMOE conjecture in the multimode case. To this end, ideas developed in [19] might be useful. We leave further exploration of this problem for future works.

Appendix A Generators of phase-covariant Gaussian channels

In this appendix we show that any single-mode phase-covariant channel given by (11) is a member of a semigroup whose Lindbladian equals (12).

Let us consider the family of channels {Φt:t≥0}\{\Phi_{t}:\,t\geq 0\} corresponding to parameters {(λt,γt):t≥0}\{(\lambda_{t},\gamma_{t}):\,t\geq 0\} in (11):

χΦt​(ρ)​(ξ)=exp⁡(−12​γt​|ξ|2)​χρ​(λt​ξ).\chi_{\Phi_{t}(\rho)}(\xi)=\exp\!\bigg(\!\!-\frac{1}{2}\gamma_{t}|\xi|^{2}\bigg)\chi_{\rho}\big(\!\sqrt{\lambda_{t}}\,\xi\big). (51)

Suppose that {Φt:t≥0}\{\Phi_{t}:\,t\geq 0\} is a semigroup which in particular means that Φ0\Phi_{0} is the identity channel corresponding to parameters γ0=0\gamma_{0}=0 and λ0=1\lambda_{0}=1. Then, the generator of this semigroup is determined by

χℒ⁡(ρ)​(ξ)=−dd​t​χΦt​(ρ)​(ξ)|t=0.\chi_{\mathcal{L}(\rho)}(\xi)=-\frac{\text{\rm{d}}}{\text{\rm{d}}t}\chi_{\Phi_{t}(\rho)}(\xi)\Big|_{t=0}.

Using (51) we compute the derivative

=−12​γ0′​tr​(ρ⁡[𝐚,[𝐚†,Dξ]])+12​λ0′​(tr​(ρ​𝐚†​[𝐚,Dξ])−tr​(ρ​𝐚​[𝐚†,Dξ]))\displaystyle=-\frac{1}{2}\gamma_{0}^{\prime}\,\text{\rm tr}\big(\rho\big[\mathbf{a},[\mathbf{a}^{\dagger},D_{\xi}]\big]\big)+\frac{1}{2}\lambda_{0}^{\prime}\Big(\text{\rm tr}\big(\rho\,\mathbf{a}^{\dagger}\big[\mathbf{a},D_{\xi}\big]\big)-\text{\rm tr}\big(\rho\,\mathbf{a}\big[\mathbf{a}^{\dagger},D_{\xi}\big]\big)\Big)

=\displaystyle= −12​(γ0′+λ0′)​ℒ0​(ρ)−12​(γ0′−λ0′)​ℒ1​(ρ),\displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}\big(\gamma^{\prime}_{0}+\lambda^{\prime}_{0}\big)\mathcal{L}_{0}(\rho)-\frac{1}{2}\big(\gamma^{\prime}_{0}-\lambda^{\prime}_{0}\big)\mathcal{L}_{1}(\rho),

where we define

ℒ0​(ρ)=12​{𝐚𝐚†,ρ}−𝐚†​ρ​𝐚andℒ1​(ρ)=12​{𝐚†​𝐚,ρ}−𝐚​ρ​𝐚†.\mathcal{L}_{0}(\rho)=\frac{1}{2}\big\{\mathbf{a}\mathbf{a}^{\dagger},\rho\big\}-\mathbf{a}^{\dagger}\rho\mathbf{a}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\mathcal{L}_{1}(\rho)=\frac{1}{2}\big\{\mathbf{a}^{\dagger}\mathbf{a},\rho\big\}-\mathbf{a}\rho\mathbf{a}^{\dagger}.

Therefore, if the channels defined by (51) form a semigroup, then the corresponding Lindbladian is equal to

ℒ⁡(ρ)=12​(γ0′+λ0′)​ℒ0​(ρ)+12​(γ0′−λ0′)​ℒ1​(ρ).\mathcal{L}(\rho)=\frac{1}{2}\big(\gamma_{0}^{\prime}+\lambda_{0}^{\prime}\big)\mathcal{L}_{0}(\rho)+\frac{1}{2}\big(\gamma_{0}^{\prime}-\lambda_{0}^{\prime}\big)\mathcal{L}_{1}(\rho). (52)

We use this equation to obtain the generator of the three classes of phase-covariant Gaussian channels.

A.1 Attenuator channels

The attenuator channel can be physically modeled by overlapping the input state and a thermal state σβ\sigma_{\beta} on a beam splitter with transmissivity λ\lambda:

Φλatt​(ρ)=tr2​(UBS,λ​(ρ⊗σβ)​UBS,λ†),\Phi^{\text{att}}_{\lambda}(\rho)=\text{\rm tr}_{2}\Big(U_{\text{BS},\lambda}(\rho\otimes\sigma_{\beta})U_{\text{BS},\lambda}^{\dagger}\Big),

where the 2-mode unitary operator UBS,λU_{\text{BS},\lambda} can be described by

{UB​S,λ†​𝐚1​UB​S,λ=λ​𝐚1+1−λ​𝐚2,UB​S,λ†​𝐚2​UB​S,λ=−1−λ​𝐚1+λ​𝐚2.\displaystyle\begin{cases}U_{BS,\lambda}^{\dagger}\mathbf{a}_{1}U_{BS,\lambda}&=\sqrt{\lambda}\,\mathbf{a}_{1}+\sqrt{1-{\lambda}}\,\mathbf{a}_{2},\\ U_{BS,\lambda}^{\dagger}\mathbf{a}_{2}U_{BS,\lambda}&=-\sqrt{1-{\lambda}}\,\mathbf{a}_{1}+\sqrt{\lambda}\,\mathbf{a}_{2}.\end{cases} (53)

Using these relations, the characteristic function of the two-mode state UBS,λ​(ρ⊗σβ)​UBS,λ†U_{\text{BS},\lambda}(\rho\otimes\sigma_{\beta})U_{\text{BS},\lambda}^{\dagger} equals

tr​(UBS,λ​(ρ⊗σβ)​UBS,λ†​Dξ1⊗Dξ2)\displaystyle\text{\rm tr}\Big(U_{\text{BS},\lambda}(\rho\otimes\sigma_{\beta})U_{\text{BS},\lambda}^{\dagger}D_{\xi_{1}}\otimes D_{\xi_{2}}\Big) =tr​(ρ⊗σβ​UBS,λ†​(Dξ1⊗Dξ2)​UBS,λ)\displaystyle=\text{\rm tr}\Big(\rho\otimes\sigma_{\beta}U_{\text{BS},\lambda}^{\dagger}(D_{\xi_{1}}\otimes D_{\xi_{2}})U_{\text{BS},\lambda}\Big)
=tr​(ρ​Dλ​ξ1−1−λ​ξ2)​tr​(σβ​D1−λ​ξ1+λ​ξ2).\displaystyle=\text{\rm tr}\Big(\!\rho D_{\sqrt{\lambda}\xi_{1}-\sqrt{1-{\lambda}}\xi_{2}}\Big)\,\text{\rm tr}\Big(\!\sigma_{\beta}D_{\sqrt{1-{\lambda}}\xi_{1}+\sqrt{\lambda}\xi_{2}}\Big).

Thus, the characteristic function of the output state of the attenuation channel is given by

χΦλatt​(ρ)​(ξ)\displaystyle\chi_{\Phi^{\text{att}}_{\lambda}(\rho)}(\xi) =χρ​(λ​ξ1−1−λ​ξ2)​χσβ​(1−λ​ξ1+λ​ξ2)|(ξ1,ξ2)=(ξ,0)\displaystyle=\chi_{\rho}\big(\sqrt{\lambda}\,\xi_{1}-\sqrt{1-{\lambda}}\,\xi_{2}\big)\,\chi_{\sigma_{\beta}}\big(\sqrt{1-{\lambda}}\,\xi_{1}+\sqrt{\lambda}\,\xi_{2}\big)\Big|_{(\xi_{1},\xi_{2})=(\xi,0)}
=χρ​(λ​ξ)​χσβ​(1−λ​ξ)\displaystyle=\chi_{\rho}\big(\sqrt{\lambda}\,\xi\big)\,\chi_{\sigma_{\beta}}\big(\sqrt{1-{\lambda}}\,\xi\big)
=exp⁡(−12​coth⁡(β/2)​(1−λ)​|ξ|2)​χρ​(λ​ξ),\displaystyle=\exp\!\Big({\!{-\frac{1}{2}\coth(\beta/2)(1-\lambda)|\xi|^{2}}}\Big)\chi_{\rho}\big(\sqrt{\lambda}\,\xi\big),

where we replace the characteristic function of the thermal state from (9).

Setting λ=λt=e−2​c​t\lambda=\lambda_{t}=e^{-2ct} with c>0c>0 in the above relation, we observe that attenuator channels {Φλtatt:t≥0}\{\Phi^{\text{att}}_{\lambda_{t}}:\,t\geq 0\} form a semigroup. Comparing the above equation with (51) also gives γt=coth⁡(β/2)​(1−λt)\gamma_{t}=\coth(\beta/2)(1-\lambda_{t}). Therefore, by plugging λ0′=−2​c\lambda_{0}^{\prime}=-2c and γ0′=2​c​coth⁡(β/2)\gamma_{0}^{\prime}=2c\coth(\beta/2) into (52), we obtain the corresponding generator

ℒ⁡(ρ)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\rho) =c⁡(coth⁡(β/2)−1)​ℒ0​(ρ)+c⁡(coth⁡(β/2)+1)​ℒ1​(ρ).\displaystyle=c\big(\!\coth(\beta/2)-1\big)\mathcal{L}_{0}(\rho)+c\big(\!\coth(\beta/2)+1\big)\mathcal{L}_{1}(\rho).

A.2 Amplifier channels

Following a similar procedure as for attenuator channels, we can derive the generator of the semigroup of amplifier channels. An amplifier channel can be modeled by applying a two-mode squeezing unitary with squeezing parameter λ≥1\lambda\geq 1 on the input state and a thermal state σβ\sigma_{\beta}, and then tracing over the second mode:

Φλamp​(ρ)=tr2​(U2S,λ​(ρ⊗σβ)​U2S,λ†).\Phi^{\text{amp}}_{\lambda}(\rho)=\text{\rm tr}_{2}\Big(U_{\text{2S},\lambda}(\rho\otimes\sigma_{\beta})U_{\text{2S},\lambda}^{\dagger}\Big).

Here, the action of the two-mode squeezing unitary can be described by

{U2​S,λ†​𝐚1​U2​S,λ=λ​𝐚1+λ−2​𝐚2†,U2​S,λ†​𝐚2​U2​S,λ=λ​𝐚2+λ−1​𝐚1†.\displaystyle\begin{cases}U_{2S,\lambda}^{\dagger}\mathbf{a}_{1}U_{2S,\lambda}&=\sqrt{\lambda}\,\mathbf{a}_{1}+\sqrt{{\lambda}-2}\,\mathbf{a}_{2}^{\dagger},\\ U_{2S,\lambda}^{\dagger}\mathbf{a}_{2}U_{2S,\lambda}&=\sqrt{\lambda}\,\mathbf{a}_{2}+\sqrt{{\lambda}-1}\,\mathbf{a}_{1}^{\dagger}.\end{cases} (54)

Using these relations, we have

U2​S,λ†​Dξ1⊗Dξ2​U2​S,λ=Dξ1​λ−ξ¯2​λ−1⊗Dξ2​λ−ξ¯1​λ−1.U_{2S,\lambda}^{\dagger}D_{\xi_{1}}\otimes D_{\xi_{2}}U_{2S,\lambda}=D_{\xi_{1}\sqrt{\lambda}-\bar{\xi}_{2}\sqrt{\lambda-1}}\otimes D_{\xi_{2}\sqrt{\lambda}-\bar{\xi}_{1}\sqrt{\lambda-1}}.

Thus, the characteristic function of the output state is given by

χΦλamp​(ρ)​(ξ)\displaystyle\chi_{\Phi^{\text{amp}}_{\lambda}(\rho)}(\xi) =χρ​(λ​ξ1−λ−1​ξ¯2)​χσβ​(λ​ξ2−λ−1​ξ¯1)|(ξ1,ξ2)=(ξ,0)\displaystyle=\chi_{\rho}\big(\sqrt{\lambda}\,\xi_{1}-\sqrt{\lambda-1}\,\bar{\xi}_{2}\big)\,\chi_{\sigma_{\beta}}\big(\sqrt{\lambda}\,\xi_{2}-\sqrt{\lambda-1}\,\bar{\xi}_{1}\big)\Big|_{(\xi_{1},\xi_{2})=(\xi,0)}
=χρ​(λ​ξ)​χσβ​(λ−1​ξ)\displaystyle=\chi_{\rho}\big(\sqrt{\lambda}\,\xi\big)\,\chi_{\sigma_{\beta}}\big(\sqrt{{\lambda}-1}\,\xi\big)
=exp⁡(−12​coth⁡(β/2)​(λ−1)​|ξ|2)​χρ​(λ​ξ),\displaystyle=\exp\!\Big(\!{{-\frac{1}{2}\coth(\beta/2)(\lambda-1)|\xi|^{2}}}\Big)\chi_{\rho}\big(\sqrt{\lambda}\,\xi\big),

where in the last line the characteristic function of the thermal state (9) is replaced.

Setting λ=λt=e2​c​t\lambda=\lambda_{t}=e^{2ct} with c>0c>0, we observe that amplifier channels {Φλtamp:t≥0}\{\Phi^{\text{amp}}_{\lambda_{t}}:\,t\geq 0\} form a semigroup. Here, γt=coth⁡(β/2)​(λt−1)\gamma_{t}=\coth(\beta/2)(\lambda_{t}-1). Thus, by plugging λ0′=2​c\lambda_{0}^{\prime}=2c and γ0′=2​c​coth⁡(β/2)\gamma_{0}^{\prime}=2c\coth(\beta/2) in (52), we obtain the generator

ℒ⁡(ρ)\displaystyle\mathcal{L}(\rho) =c⁡(coth⁡(β/2)+1)​ℒ0​(ρ)+c⁡(coth⁡(β/2)−1)​ℒ1​(ρ).\displaystyle=c\big(\!\coth(\beta/2)+1\big)\mathcal{L}_{0}(\rho)+c\big(\!\coth(\beta/2)-1\big)\mathcal{L}_{1}(\rho).

Note that here we get the same coefficients as those of the generator of the attenuator semigroup, but swapped.

A.3 Additive-noise channels

The classical additive-noise Gaussian channels can be modeled by applying a displacement operator whose parameter is chosen at random according to a Gaussian probability distribution:

Φγadd​(ρ)=2π​γ​∫e−2γ​|α|2​Dα​ρ​Dα†​d2​α.\Phi^{\text{add}}_{\gamma}(\rho)=\frac{2}{\pi\gamma}\int e^{-\frac{2}{\gamma}|\alpha|^{2}}D_{\alpha}\rho D^{\dagger}_{\alpha}\,\text{\rm{d}}^{2}\alpha.

The characteristic function of the output state of this channel is given by

χΦγadd​(ρ)​(ξ)\displaystyle\chi_{\Phi^{\text{add}}_{\gamma}(\rho)}(\xi) =2π​γ​∫e−2γ​|α|2​tr​(Dα​ρ​Dα†​Dξ)​d2​α\displaystyle=\frac{2}{\pi\gamma}\int e^{-\frac{2}{\gamma}|\alpha|^{2}}\text{\rm tr}\big(D_{\alpha}\rho D^{\dagger}_{\alpha}D_{\xi}\big)\,\text{\rm{d}}^{2}\alpha
=2π​γ​χρ​(ξ)​∫e−2γ​|α|2​eξ​α¯−ξ¯​α​d2​α\displaystyle=\frac{2}{\pi\gamma}\chi_{\rho}(\xi)\int e^{-\frac{2}{\gamma}|\alpha|^{2}}e^{\xi\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\xi}\alpha}\,\text{\rm{d}}^{2}\alpha
=exp⁡(−12​γ​|ξ|2)​χρ​(ξ),\displaystyle=\exp\!\Big({-\frac{1}{2}\gamma|\xi|^{2}}\Big)\chi_{\rho}(\xi),

where we use Dα†​Dξ​Dα=exp⁡(ξ​α¯−ξ¯​α)​DξD^{\dagger}_{\alpha}D_{\xi}D_{\alpha}=\exp(\xi\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\xi}\alpha)D_{\xi} in the second line.

By choosing γ=2​c​t\gamma=2ct with c>0c>0, the channels {Φtadd:t≥0}\{\Phi^{\text{add}}_{t}:\,t\geq 0\} form a semigroup. Here, λt=1\lambda_{t}=1. Thus, by inserting λ0′=0\lambda_{0}^{\prime}=0 and γ0′=2​c\gamma_{0}^{\prime}=2c in (52) we obtain the generator

ℒ⁡(ρ)=c​ℒ0​(ρ)+c​ℒ1​(ρ).\mathcal{L}(\rho)=c\mathcal{L}_{0}(\rho)+c\mathcal{L}_{1}(\rho).

In this appendix we show that Υ⁡(ρ)\Upsilon(\rho) given by

is well-defined for any state ρ\rho with finite mean photon number. For such a state both tr​(ρ​𝐚†​𝐚),tr​(ρ​𝐚𝐚†)\text{\rm tr}(\rho\mathbf{a}^{\dagger}\mathbf{a}),\text{\rm tr}(\rho\mathbf{a}\mathbf{a}^{\dagger}) are finite. ≤∑i,j(1p​λi+1p^​λj)​|⟨ψi|𝐚|ψj⟩|2\displaystyle\leq\sum_{i,j}\Big(\frac{1}{p}\lambda_{i}+\frac{1}{\hat{p}}\lambda_{j}\Big)\big|\langle\psi_{i}|\mathbf{a}|\psi_{j}\rangle\big|^{2}

Therefore, since tr​(ρ​𝐚†​𝐚)\text{\rm tr}\big(\rho\mathbf{a}^{\dagger}\mathbf{a}\big) is finite, S⁡(ρ)S(\rho) is also finite.
